verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Foreign Office travel advisory (19 Aug 2026), as covered by Sahara Reporters, warns LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation, stating that same-sex sexual activity is illegal with penalties of up to 14 years' imprisonment, and that the federal law extends beyond those entering same-sex marriages to people who help arrange or conduct such events, attend events perceived to be same-sex weddings, or are involved with gay groups - including helping to register or organise them or publicly promoting same-sex relationships. It adds that some northern states operate Sharia law under which same-sex activity can attract the death penalty, without naming which states - consistent with this record's finding that no audited source places Taraba among them, while the federal penalties and arrest-risk warnings apply state-wide. National-framework facts the record's own summary claims for this state.

UK Foreign Office travel advisory (19 Aug 2026), as covered by Sahara Reporters, warns LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation, stating that same-sex sexual activity is illegal with penalties of up to 14 years' imprisonment, and that the federal law extends beyond those entering same-sex marriages to people who help arrange or conduct such events, attend events perceived to be same-sex weddings, or are involved with gay groups - including helping to register or organise them or publicly promoting same-sex relationships. It adds that some northern states operate Sharia law under which same-sex activity can attract the death penalty - a warning that does not reach this southern state, while the federal penalties and arrest-risk warnings apply in full. The Diplomat (14 Aug 2026, Robin Vochelet) supplies the national-picture evidence this division's assessment at the national score rests on: Indonesia lacks explicitly anti-LGBTQ+ laws, yet legal frameworks indirectly discriminate and same-sex sexual activity can be criminalised under moral laws; in July 2026 a wave of hate crimes targeted transgender women across the country - in Bogor (West Java) more than 15 trans women were doused with urine, forced to strip naked and physically beaten, with online commenters calling for further attacks. President Prabowo Subianto's October 2025 presidential decree listed LGBTQ+ issues among nonmilitary threats in national security policy, steps toward codifying anti-LGBTQ+ attitudes into law.
